stimulus.text: In July 1775, the Second Continental Congress sent the Olive Branch Petition to King George III. The petition affirmed loyalty to the king and blamed the troubles on Parliament, proposing that the colonies govern themselves more freely within the empire. George III rejected the petition without reading it. Historians estimate that about 40 to 45 percent of colonists were Patriots who wanted independence, about 15 to 20 percent were Loyalists who wanted to keep ties with Britain, and the rest did not strongly support either side.
stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question; the figures follow Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 5.

books.section: B. Common Sense, the Declaration of Independence, and Republican Self-Government

stem: What do the historians' estimates in the passage — about 40 to 45 percent Patriots, 15 to 20 percent Loyalists — most clearly show about independence in 1775-1776?

options.text: That nearly every colonist had already chosen independence by 1775
options.misconception: About half the colonists were Patriots or Loyalists combined — the rest were uncommitted, so nearly every colonist had not chosen.

options.text: That Loyalists outnumbered Patriots and blocked independence
options.misconception: Patriots outnumbered Loyalists by about two to one. The Loyalists did not block independence.

options.text: That independence was not a foregone conclusion, with a large middle uncommitted
That the uncommitted colonists were mostly enslaved people with no voice
options.misconception: Background: the uncommitted were colonists of all kinds who had not taken a side — the passage does not say they were mostly enslaved.

rationales.C: With 40 to 45 percent Patriots and 15 to 20 percent Loyalists, roughly two-fifths of colonists stood uncommitted — Background: independence had to be won, not assumed. The middle had to be persuaded, and the war persuaded it.
rationales.A: The figures show the opposite: a large share of colonists had not chosen a side by 1775.
rationales.B: Patriots outnumbered Loyalists. The Loyalists were the smaller group, not the blocking majority.
rationales.D: The passage does not describe the uncommitted as mostly enslaved. They were colonists who had not strongly supported either side.
rationales.general:
1. Add up the committed. Patriots at 40 to 45 percent plus Loyalists at 15 to 20 percent leave a large remainder.
2. Name the remainder. Roughly two-fifths of colonists had not strongly supported either side.
3. Read what that means. Background: independence was argued for and won over time — it was not decided in advance.
Remember: when the numbers leave a large middle, the outcome was contested — count the uncommitted before calling anything inevitable.
